title: Swap operations require a maxSlippage limit because volume caps cannot bound value lost to execution price
content:
The Swap Rate Limits at A.6.1.1.2.2.6.1.3.1.12.1.2.4.3 and A.6.1.1.2.2.6.1.3.1.12.3.2.4.3 carry a third parameter absent from every deposit and withdrawal limit in this chunk: `maxSlippage`: 0.1%.

The reason is structural, not incidental. A deposit into a lending pool or a stablecoin conduit exchanges value at or near par — the quantity moved is a faithful proxy for the risk taken, so `maxAmount` and `slope` are sufficient controls. A swap moves value *through a price*, so an unbounded-price swap of a bounded quantity can still destroy an unbounded fraction of that quantity. Volume limits are blind to that loss.

This makes `maxSlippage` a categorically different kind of control from the other two: `maxAmount` bounds burst size, `slope` bounds sustained flow, and `maxSlippage` bounds *quality of execution*. It is the only one of the three that defends against adversarial conditions at the venue — a manipulated pool, a sandwich attack, or simply thin liquidity — rather than against Grove's own over-allocation.

A.6.1.1.2.2.6.1.3.1.12.1.2.4.1 makes the complementarity explicit by setting the Swaps Instance's deposit and withdrawal limits to "N/A - swaps only." Where the operation is purely an exchange, the quantity limits are inapplicable and the slippage bound plus a swap volume limit carry the entire control burden.
description: Grove's Uniswap Instances add maxSlippage to the usual maxAmount/slope pair; deposit and withdrawal conduits move value at par, so only swaps can destroy value at constant volume.
